analysis: Portfolio is essentially fully deployed ($3,113 available cash vs $100K+ in three open positions), leaving no meaningful capital to add a new position without violating sizing rules. Current positions: MSFT is working well (+4.77%) and remains in the screened candidate list; MCO is flat (-0.32%) and not on the screened list (likely failed trend filter); V is underwater (-2.73%) and also not on the screened list, warranting close stop monitoring. With only $3,112 in cash, any new position would be trivially small — the 1-2% portfolio risk rule requires $1,035-$2,070 at risk, which for typical 6-10% stops on quality names implies position sizes of $10K-$35K, far exceeding available liquidity. Forcing a $3K micro-position creates administrative overhead without meaningful return contribution. Screened candidates show several interesting setups (ZBRA: PEG 0.53, basing at 35% of 52w range; FDS: fwd P/E 12.79, ROE 28%, basing at 24% of range; ADP: ROE 71%, basing uptrend), but these require capital we do not currently have. The correct action is to hold cash, monitor existing stops — particularly V which is approaching thesis-break territory — and wait for a position to exit before redeploying into higher-conviction candidates. The ADSK loss (-3.69%) reinforces the need for patience. Cash is a position; forcing a sub-scale trade to stay active is the enemy of compounding.
